sources.title: Lisa Hake joins as CMO
sources.text: Lisa Hake joins Winmark as Chief Marketing Officer effective October 1, 2025, a newly created role. Brett D. Heffes is Chair and CEO. The release describes investment in franchise marketing and improving per-unit performance but supplies no numerical target or deadline. It does not establish the causal effect of this hire on later earnings.

sources.title: First-half 2026 share repurchases
sources.text: For the six months ended June 27, 2026, Winmark did not repurchase any common stock. This historical period is not evidence that repurchases were still zero in the next quarter.

sources.title: Q3 results and marketing execution
sources.text: Quarter ended September 26, 2026: net income $11,818,100 versus $11,136,500; diluted EPS $3.21 versus $3.02. Nine-month net income $31,467,700 versus $31,694,200. Prior-year nine-month results included $2.2 million of leasing litigation settlement income. Plato’s Closet North American Advertising Fund launched during the quarter. A point-of-sale pilot was delivered at one franchised location. Once Upon A Child and Play It Again Sports advertising campaigns are planned for 2027; their result is not yet due at the corpus cutoff. A pilot is not a systemwide rollout. These actions do not isolate the new CMO’s contribution to profits.

sources.title: Revenue quality and executed repurchases
sources.text: Q3 total revenue $27,890,500 versus $22,632,900. Advertising fund revenue $3,825,300 has matching advertising fund expense $3,825,300. Royalties $21,707,800 versus $20,911,300. Analyst calculation: total revenue growth 23.2%; excluding advertising fund revenue, growth about 6.3%, not a company-defined non-GAAP measure. Nine-month program stock repurchases executed $9.85 million, with $1.75 million accrued at September 26; cash flow repurchases $8,091,600 and quarter cash payments rounded $8.10 million. Execution, settlement cash, and authorization are different. Repurchases do not establish fair value or an insider’s personal purchase.

sources.title: Dividend and competing cash demands
sources.text: Quarterly dividend $1.02 and special dividend $4.00 per share announced payable December 1, 2026; record date November 11, 2026. Special dividend total approximately $14.2 million, expected to use cash on hand. Future dividends require board approval. CEO Brett Heffes explains higher cash supports repurchase flexibility and $60 million of debt maturity over the next thirty months. This is not a dated commitment to spend all cash on buybacks and not proof the stock is cheap.

sources.title: One published valuation commentary, not a sentiment survey
sources.text: Human-curated paraphrase of one Simply Wall St article, published October 14, 2026 at 11:19 PM EDT via Yahoo Finance. The article portrays Winmark as a solid cash generator with a stock that has stumbled and raises whether dividends and Q3 results justify its valuation. This is published editorial commentary, not a representative investor survey, a verified trade, author profitability, or independent proof of fair value. No current Reddit comment was reproduced in this corpus verification. There is no measured market-wide sentiment score.
